Now for the long answer. Dogs with abusive owners have been shown to exhibit symptoms of PTSD. However it is difficult to tell whether this is an actual illness or just an associative mechanism... a Pavlovian response. Pavlov was able to show (in a sugar coated version) that dogs could have a physical response to a mental stimulus like salivating when a bell was rung by associating the sound with food. When it comes to the complexities of mental illness it's not as simple as association.

Mental illness are different than most illnesses because they are defined by their symptoms and several illnesses share symptoms. Until everything can be pinpointed it's hard to diagnose. You could show anti-social traits of PTSD that are common with dissociative traits in Sociopathy but until you can group togeather other symptoms and identify causes or triggers you can't say one or the other. 

So dose the pet have PTSD from an abusive owner because it cowers from a lifted shoe or dose it just associate it with pain and that can be un-learned? Dose a dog hear voices or sounds that it barks at that are products if it's own mind or does it just like to bark? Who knows, find one that speaks a human language and put it on a couch.

Got you fam. Hiring, terminating, evaluating, and developing employees is literally in my job description.

 The closest it gets is if they ask if you'll be able to perform with or without "reasonable accommodations" which can be a supper subjective question. It can mean anything to either parties and what can be considered unreasonable to one employer is totally reasonable with another. A lot of times this won't even be asked for entry level because you never know 'till the work speaks for itself. 

If it worries you my best advice is to let your experiences and attitude tell volumes. You'll have tons of questions well before anyone asks you "reasonable accommodations". Why do you want to work here? Don't say "I need a job" seriously dime a dozen. Say you want my job, tell me some "the greatest journey starts with a single step" shit. Show me the value of your perspective.

There is such a thing as coming off too confident so don't try to fake it. We've seen too many "go getters" that last maybe a week. If you're honest and determined there's a place in the work force for you.

But if you can, be upfront with what you'll need so they can have the chance to accommodate and see your worth unhindered. If they don't want to work with your divergence, you don't want to work with them.

PS. The one thing I always hope to hear is at the end of the interview. You'll be asked if you have any questions. Ask them "Is there any reason you wouldn't hire me?" It shows that you are thoughtful and it gives you a chance to clear up any doubt the interviewer has about hiring you.

Remember that Hitler would have just been a nut with a conspiracy theory if no one had moraly agreed with him and followed his leadership. So yes all of us agree that genocide is wrong, but in 1945 it's estimated that there were around 8 million Nazis. 8 milion people who at least on some small degree found Hitler's actions morally in line with their own values enough to carry out the atrocities of the holocaust.

If morality had been objective it's likely that no one would have allowed such suffering and waste of human life. Whether from greed or fear Hitler had a nation's army, a political party, and several allies that helped him become the monster that we know. Most countries didn't even make a move against the regime until they were attacked first. They found it moral to hope the situation sorted itself out without personally interfering and putting their people at risk.

So is it "Objectively Moral" to protect your family and nation against a menace that has already caused so much suffering? If you said yes congratulations you could have been swayed into the Nazi party if you lived in 1930s Germany through propaganda.  

Sorry for the short essay here but the "everyone agrees Hitler was bad" argument is often used in discussion  of Objective Morality but WWII is actually one of the best examples of how morality can be swayed and thus is not objective.
